Incorporating April 2019 SLOOS, the FOMC’s cautiously positive baseline is tempered by evidence of tightening credit supply and softer loan demand. Banks reported tightening standards for C&I loans and for construction and land development loans, and tightened other terms across borrower sizes. Demand was weaker for HELOCs, credit cards, other consumer loans, and for construction/land development, while auto and subprime mortgage demand was broadly unchanged. These signals point to a modest headwind for business investment, CRE activity, and household credit, reinforcing the FOMC’s note of “soft” business fixed investment and heightened uncertainties despite a strong labor market and below-target inflation. Netting these, the outlook remains slightly positive but more two-sided, warranting a more cautious stance than the initial read.
